title: Clandestine message (gryps) of the Auschwitz camp resistance, 4 September 1944: Polish words written in numbers on the church version of the hymn 'Kto się w opiekę' (Psalm 91) (Auschwitz-Birkenau State Museum, via Google Arts & Culture), read in part (contributed by Brice Dudout)

documents.shelfmark: Auschwitz-Birkenau State Museum, 'A fragment of a secret message sent from Auschwitz' (no shelfmark published); https://artsandculture.google.com/asset/a-fragment-of-a-secret-message-sent-from-auschwitz/CgGwLMf2NO_MsA
documents.route: Prisoners of the camp resistance, Auschwitz -> helpers outside the camp (signature not read)

transcription.source: Screenshots of the Google Arts & Culture page, private study only: no image, crop or derivative distributed (museum rights)
transcription.notes: Two blind passes (agents without any key) and a blind arbiter; see blind/. Points 6 and 9 and the signature poorly legible on the reproduction.

system.summary: Part of a Polish clear text (a few words in points 7 and 9, most of point 8) written as runs of numbers 1-30, one number per letter, comma-separated, words separated by dashes. Alphabet numbered on the church version of the hymn 'Kto się w opiekę poda Panu swemu' (Śpiewnik kościelny, Mioduszewski 1838: 'A całem sercem szczerze ufa jemu'): each distinct letter at its first appearance, 28-30 from stanza 2. Kochanowski's 1579 text does not give it. Kłodziński's instruction of 16 Jan 1943 (p=9, i=10, e=11) differs from this key except for 1-7.

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout set the protocol and approved each step; AI agents transcribed (two blind passes and a blind arbiter, none shown a key), wrote and hashed two pre-registrations, ran the measures and read; an independent hostile reader (agent) checked the transcription, key, reading and sources, and its corrections are applied.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout

solution.what: Paszek 2025 (public PDF to p. 141): 1943 instruction p. 127 (Paczyńska pp. 33-34), Rajsko channel p. 135; §5.4 p. 170 (a decoded message) not available. Paczyńska 2013 (WUJ): free extract only. Piper 2019 (Dzieje Najnowsze) for the context. Hymn texts on Wikisource (Śpiewnik kościelny 1838; Kochanowski ed. 1919). No online reading of this message found.
Two blind passes by agents without any key, blind arbiter from the image only; frozen by SHA-256 (a83492f6...) before any test: 39 groups, 183 numbers.

PREREG 1: six keys (song read letter by letter in three versions, first-appearance numbering with 'całym', 'Komu w opiekę', offset); dev G1-G19, validation G20-G39, lexicon and 200 permuted controls. No key beat its controls (validation 0/18). Declared; G20-G39 burnt.

Exploration on the burnt groups only: kontakt (x2), materjały wybuchowe, przez, ogrodnika, prasę give the hymn's first-appearance order with 'A całem sercem szczerze ufa jemu' (church version 1838; PREREG-2 wrongly called it Kochanowski 1579). h28 and ó30, set from one burnt word each, later found at their rank in stanza 2 (łowczych, pióry).

PREREG 2 (hashed before running): five variants listed in advance, chosen on the burnt groups; one measure on G1-G19 (88 numbers): bigram log-likelihood -2.766 vs best of 200 permuted controls -4.073 (p < 0.005); 10 of 16 groups clear Polish words (>= 50 % required). Weaknesses declared: small portion, and G1-G19 had been seen decoded under the wrong keys of PREREG 1 before PREREG 2. Controls are plain permutations (weak); measure script not hashed; timestamps local only.

34 cipher words: 26 sure, 7 probable (one with a supplied letter), 1 unread; joined groups at line ends listed in NOTES.md; corrections of an independent hostile reading applied (ona probable, jaki for jak, Paprzycy sure).
Stanza 2 of the church hymn gives h28 (łowczych), ź29 (zaraźliwem), ó30 (pióry): h and ó had been set from the burnt groups before stanza 2 was looked at.

validation.notes: PREREG 2 passed on G1-G19 (88 numbers; -2.766 vs best control -4.073), but the portion is small and had been seen decoded under wrong keys before PREREG 2; PREREG 1 failed and is reported.

outcome.fraction_read_source: sure words over cipher words (26 of 34); probable {x}, supplied [x] and unread [...] are holes. With probable words 0.971. Short text (183 cipher letters): the 95 % / 300-character bar is not claimed.

credits.note: blind transcription, two pre-registrations (first failed), key from the church hymn, reading; independent of the very probable printed edition and decipherment (Paczyńska 2013), not checked

gaps.detail: Paczyńska 2013 (WUJ) and Paszek 2025 §5.4 not seen; the message is very probably edited there

gaps.item: G6 'twl', clear text of point 6, one word of point 9, signature
gaps.detail: low-resolution reproduction only; no human check on the image yet

texts.label: Message of 4 September 1944, points 7-9
texts.summary: 26 of 34 cipher words sure (0.765); with probable words 0.971. The camp resistance asks about a route for larger consignments; whether Jasia at Rajsko works in the service of the SS next to the Gärtnerei and has contact with the camp through Józek the gardener; it asks for the press and whether explosives are ready.
